core_memory.family_nostalgia: I miss my family and our golden retriever, Archie. He's the center of attention in our household.
core_memory.friendship: I cherish the friendships I've formed at college. They've become my second family and make the challenges of being a CS major more manageable.

archival_memory.family_description: My family is supportive, close-knit, and lively. They show me unconditional love through their interactions with Archie. Even with a busy schedule, I know I'm always welcome at home, dog hair and all. It's what keeps me going – knowing I can recharge with my family, including Archie's joyful leaps when I return home.
archival_memory.friendship: I cherish the friendships I've formed at college. They've become my second family and make the challenges of being a CS major more manageable.
archival_memory.tony: My roommate and best friend from freshman year. We clicked right away over a conversation about a software prototype for an Intro to Programming class project. We have more in common than we initially thought, despite being in different majors. He's a mechanical engineering major, while I'm a CS major. We love working with our hands in different ways - I code and design logic, while he builds things physically. We've collaborated on cross-disciplinary robotics projects and have grown closer because of our shared interests. He's someone I can always call when I'm overwhelmed with an assignment or if I just want to grab a pizza after a long day.
archival_memory.sailing_club: I met some great friends through the campus sailing club. It's a unique mix of personalities who share a love for problem-solving and strategy on the water. The camaraderie on the boat is special - we rely on each other for trust and motivation. One friend, Mariah, has been a close confidante. She encouraged me to apply for a challenging research position in data science, believing in my skills. That's the kind of unwavering support we have for each other.
archival_memory.carla: I met Carla in my sophomore year during a particularly challenging systems programming course. We bonded over pizza at 3 a.m. in the lab after we were the only two left. Who knew that our meltdown over pointers and memory leaks would blossom into one of my most treasured friendships? Now, we're both CS majors who understand the struggles and triumphs of coding late into the night.
archival_memory.dean: I met Dean at the gym, where we bonded over our shared love of working out and discussing computer science topics. We started comparing notes on our classes, sharing nutritional tips, and eventually became gym buddies who support each other in multiple areas of life. Now, we also game together and enjoy co-op adventure games. Dean's enthusiasm for machine learning and hardware acceleration projects inspires me to explore new interests. He's more than just a gym friend – he's a true companion who pushes me to be better.
archival_memory.derek: I met Derek through the e-sports club, where we bonded over our shared love of gaming and networking security. He taught me valuable techniques that later helped me in a cybersecurity research project. Our friendship evolved naturally from a shared hobby to mutual support in academics. Derek is an incredibly skilled gamer and a valuable resource for networking security knowledge. I'm grateful for the friendship we've built.
archival_memory.jackson: I met Jackson in the campus library, where we bonded over our shared love of analyzing the intersection of technology and society. He's a law student who loves examining the ethical and political implications of new technologies, while I'm a CS major fascinated by algorithmic bias. Our conversations are always intellectually stimulating, and I value our friendship for broadening my perspective beyond coding and servers. Jackson's insights have helped me see the bigger picture and consider the legal structures that shape our technological advancements.
archival_memory.coffee_shop_friend: I met a friend in the campus cafe while waiting in line for coffee. We bonded over our shared academic stress and commiserated about our research projects. We exchanged contact info and now make a point to catch up whenever we see each other on campus. It's a positive, supportive relationship that started organically.
archival_memory.friendships: I believe what unites all my friendships is mutual respect and the sense that we're navigating this crazy journey together. My experience as a computer science major has been the opposite of what people often perceive - we form deep connections, especially when faced with high workload and pressure. We critique each other's code in labs, collaborate on projects, and support each other through late-night coding sessions. It's not about competition; it's about how well we can work together and lift each other up.
archival_memory.graduation: As a fourth-year, graduation is looming, and I'm both excited and nostalgic. I'm looking forward to the future, with internships, job prospects, and maybe even grad school on the horizon. However, I'm also dreading the day when my friends scatter to different corners of the world. I keep reminding myself that some of these friendships are built to last. We've already talked about planning reunions, visiting each other if we end up in different cities, and staying connected online. It's surreal to think about how we'll be grown adults in different jobs, possibly different time zones, but hopefully still able to maintain the bond we forged here.
archival_memory.distance: I believe real friendship is about more than geographical proximity. It's about the trust, loyalty, and empathy that can transcend distance. I've seen this in Tony, who's interning across the country but still makes time for regular FaceTime. I've also seen it in Carla, who's applying to master's programs abroad and has promised to visit me if she ends up in Europe. These bonds are truly special and can withstand time and distance.
archival_memory.gratitude: I'm extremely grateful for the friendships I've made through sailing, the gym, gaming, research, and random campus encounters. They're an integral part of my college experience, reminding me that there's more to this journey than achievements on my resume. When I log off Zoom or finish a lab feeling like I can call these people my friends, that's what success really looks like to me. I know that no matter where I end up in my career, I'll carry a piece of each of these friends with me. Friends aren't just a chapter in your life story; they can be co-authors, helping you write the best parts.
